sections.h2: How can a Carrollton homeowner sell, and which route is quickest?
sections.html:
Carrollton owners have three choices: engage an agent, go it alone, or turn the keys over to a cash buyer who accepts the property untouched. Condition, timing and any tenant or co-owner complications steer the choice.

  • Agent listing: the biggest buyer pool, along with showings, inspection requests and lender deadlines.
  • Private sale: no listing agent, though pricing and paperwork land on you.
  • Cash purchase: fewer steps and no repair demands, at a price usually below a polished listing.

Renters outnumber owners in Carrollton. Homeownership stands at 41.0 percent for 2020-2024 in Census data, and just 73.9 percent of people lived at the same address twelve months earlier, which signals frequent moves.

sections.h2: How did the University of West Georgia grow out of Carrollton?
sections.html:
The University of West Georgia occupies the western side of Carrollton, and its story starts in the city. A 1906 state law created agricultural and mechanical schools for each congressional district. In 1907, trustees bought the 275-acre Bluford Sharp farm west of town for $9,625 as the Fourth District A&M School site, and classes began in January 1908 under the motto 'We Learn to Do by Doing.' The library's timeline notes that only two automobiles were in Carrollton when the school opened, a reminder of how much the town has changed. In the 1950s the college drew attention beyond Georgia for its adult education program, which was then called College in the Community.

After the Board of Regents picked the Carrollton campus on April 15, 1933, it became West Georgia College. It turned into the State University of West Georgia in 1996 and the University of West Georgia on January 12, 2005, according to the university library's timeline. A small reminder of the town-campus link: the campus chapel was built in 1893 in downtown Carrollton and moved to the grounds in 1964.

Campus influence fades with distance. Before assuming student demand reaches your block, ask a local agent or investor how far your house sits from it.

sections.h2: How does Carrollton compare with the country on housing and income?
sections.html:
Carrollton had an estimated 27,925 residents in mid-2025, up 4.5 percent from its 2020 base, across 22.41 square miles of land. The measures below cover 2020-2024.

The numbers are from the Census tables for Carrollton and the United States. House values sit a little under the national midpoint, while incomes and rents sit well under it. Owners with a mortgage pay a midpoint $1,590 a month, against $1,963 nationally, and 88.5 percent of households have broadband. Owners with no mortgage carry a midpoint $632 a month, close to the $638 national figure, so the cost of holding a paid-off house in Carrollton is much like anywhere else. With poverty at 25.4 percent, affordability limits many local buyers, and a house needing work may lose more value in a retail sale than the repair would cost.

Household details: 9,992 households average 2.45 people each, income per person is $32,873 in 2024 dollars, children make up about a fifth of the population, seniors about an eighth, and 759 residents are veterans. Other Census entries: roughly 35 percent of adults have a four-year degree, nine in a hundred were born abroad, and 2022 retail sales reached $34,866 for each resident against $20,928 nationally, which points to a shopping and service hub for the surrounding area.

sections.h2: Which public schools serve Carrollton houses?
sections.html:
Carrollton City Schools operates its own district, which describes four schools on a single 130-acre campus: Carrollton Elementary, Carrollton Upper Elementary, Carrollton Middle School and Carrollton High.

Whether an address lies inside that district depends on the city limits, so confirm it with the school system before putting it in a listing. Parents tend to ask about schools first, and a correct answer helps a serious buyer move faster. The city system's schools are all on one campus, which some families treat as a selling point.

sections.h2: What does Carrollton require for short-term rentals?
sections.html:
Carrollton added a short-term rental article to its code in July 2025, as Chapter 18, Article VI. The code defines a short-term rental as a dwelling, or part of one, rented for lodging for 30 consecutive days or fewer, and no one may rent without a license.

  • The license is annual, with a non-refundable $500 application fee filed with Community Development.
  • Occupancy tops out at two adults per bedroom, with one vehicle per bedroom parked on paved surfaces, never on the street.
  • External signs are banned, and the license number must appear on every online listing.
  • Three convictions or judgments for code violations trigger a 12-month revocation.
  • Appeals of a denial, suspension or revocation go in writing to the Mayor and City Council within 30 calendar days.

Hotel-motel tax applies as well. Each license is tied to one owner and one address, so a buyer planning a rental must obtain a new one. The city's licensing and permit office, which also handles code enforcement, occupational tax and alcohol licensing, answers questions at 770-830-2000. The ordinance states that rentals remain subject to occupational tax, regulatory fees, business licenses and the zoning ordinance, so check where your parcel is zoned before listing it to investors.

sections.h2: How do Carroll County assessments and tax bills affect a Carrollton sale?
sections.html:
The county, not the city, appraises and bills Carrollton property. Its tax page sets out the basics: each parcel's fair market value is fixed on January 1, assessment is 40 percent of that, and a mill is one dollar per thousand dollars of assessed value. Rates come from several bodies: commissioners for county operations, the school board for schools, and the state, capped at a quarter mill.

An appeal begins at the county assessors' board, and may continue to the Board of Equalization, a panel the grand jury appoints. Filers can choose arbitration instead. Georgia notices carry a 45-day appeal window, so rely on the date printed on yours. In Carroll County the Board of Assessors takes returns and homestead applications, while the tax commissioner prepares and collects bills; call 770-830-5843 about calculations, late payments and interest, or 770-830-5826 for the tag and tax office.

Before you accept an offer, gather the papers a buyer will request: the latest assessment notice, any lease and rent ledger, a copy of a short-term rental license if one exists, and permits for past work. Georgia's transfer tax also applies to the sale. The rate is a dollar on the first thousand of price plus a dime for each further hundred or fraction, and the seller bears the cost unless the contract provides otherwise. For exemption questions, contact the Carroll County superior court clerk.

faqs.q: Do most Carrollton households own their homes?
faqs.a: No. Census data show homeownership at 41.0 percent for 2020-2024, against 65.2 percent nationally, so most households rent.
About 27,900: 27,925 in the mid-2025 estimate, up from 26,738 in the 2020 census and 24,388 in 2010.

faqs.q: Do Airbnb-style rentals need a license in Carrollton?
faqs.a: Yes. For stays of 30 consecutive days or fewer, the city requires an annual license with a $500 non-refundable application fee, and the license cannot pass to a new owner.

faqs.q: Which office bills property tax on a Carrollton house?
faqs.a: Carroll County. Its assessors set the values, and the county tax commissioner prepares bills, collects payment and answers questions at 770-830-5843.

faqs.q: Is a tenant-occupied Carrollton house sellable?
faqs.a: Yes. A buyer who pays cash and accepts the house as-is can take it subject to the lease. Share the lease terms early, and find out from your closing professional how deposits and prepaid rent are handled.
